acceptanceCriteria: Each changed package keeps its descendant-cleanup test passing, and a test for the shared helper shows the group is signalled before the leader is reaped.

Every listed runner signals its process group before reaping the leader where waitid is available, reusing or matching gokernel's waitGroupLeader, and keeps its existing timeout, cancellation and error classification.
The gitrun_unix.go comment matches the order the code uses.
body: Found 2026-09-26 while diagnosing the v0-6 gate load flakes. Seven runners SIGKILL the child's process group (kill(-pid)) only after Wait has reaped the leader: internal/contextindex/git.go:231 (deferred terminateProcessGroup), internal/doccompiler/process.go:85 (deferred), internal/cem/gitrun/gitrun.go:250 (killDescendants after the reap; gitrun_unix.go:16-17 says the kill happens before the reap), internal/liveverify/mutate/shared.go:43 and gotest.go:180 (after Run), internal/taskman/process_unix.go:37 (after Run), internal/worksource/git.go:214 (deferred cleanupGitProcess), and internal/releasegate/git_unix.go:59 (after Wait). Once the leader is reaped and no descendant keeps its group alive, the group ID can name an unrelated process group whose leader reused that PID, so the sweep can kill it. The window is narrow (a reused PID that is also a group leader), so the severity is low. internal/gokernel/process_unix.go already fixes this with waitGroupLeader, which signals the group while the exited leader is still unreaped (waitid WNOWAIT) and falls back to the old order elsewhere. V1-0312 lists only the contextindex site among its unverified items.
title: Signal the process group before reaping in the remaining Git and tool runners
